findings.text: the construction-site guard cannot fail on the wrapper case it exists to catch: a decorator or a further partial layer around functools.partial(_persisting_quorum_cycles, **kwargs) at either workers.py call site (8987, 11113) leaves the inner partial(...) Call intact in the module's AST, so _persisting_partial_construction_sites still returns two keyword-carrying Call nodes and 'assert len(sites) == 2' passes while the site no longer builds the callable the seam recognises. The runtime loss is a refused incumbent recorded as a skipped audit (cascade.py:593 catches it and stores the reason), not a canonical write, so this is a lost review-time signal rather than a safety hole.

the group-id assertion is not independent of the value under test: the test injects review_group_id into a fabricated panel_result and reads the same value back off the record, so it reddens on the declared control (dropping the field from record.update) but cannot detect the regression fix 2 exists to prevent at its source - a quorum verdict that stops returning review_group_id, in which case panel_audit.py:136 _audit_group_id silently mints an unrelated uuid and the row no longer names the cycle it observed. No test drives the real _run_rd_quorum_cycles (workers.py:8016, whose return at workers.py:8513 is where the id comes from) and asserts the row's group id equals the id its cycle rows carry; the graph test at :621 feeds the id in from above for the same reason, and :538 asserts only that a skipped row's id is truthy, which any uuid satisfies.
